result.title: Could This BE Any More Wrong? Teaching VLMs to Know What They Don't Know in Document Extraction
result.comment: 11 pages, 6 figures, 10 tables. Accepted at the AI4Finance Summit at ICAIF '26 (7th ACM International Conference on AI in Finance), Milan, Italy. An extended version with a revised experimental protocol will follow
result.summary: Vision-Language Models can extract structured fields from scanned financial documents, yet they provide no indication of when a field might be wrong. We derive per-field confidence estimates from the token log-probabilities the model already produces, via a token-to-span alignment procedure that maps logprobs onto each extracted value within the structured JSON output. Evaluated on two benchmarks (CORD v2 receipts, Kleister NDA legal contracts) with three VLM families, the minimum token probability per field achieves Area Under the ROC Curve (AUROC) 0.74-0.91 for error detection, far exceeding verbalized confidence (0.53-0.56). The uncertain fields form a natural training curriculum: fine-tuning via Group Relative Policy Optimisation (GRPO) improves accuracy from 78.5% to 87.5% on CORD (67 examples) and from 70.7% to 75.1% on multi-page NDA contracts (259 examples), while substantially improving error detection on Kleister NDA (AUROC 0.70 to 0.85, Area Under the Accuracy-Rejection Curve (AUARC) 0.78 to 0.92). The loop requires no annotation beyond the training-split ground truth, demonstrating that confidence-guided curriculum selection transfers to complex multi-page documents when combined with native multi-image training. A frontier model (Claude Sonnet 4) used as a pseudo-label judge achieves ~92% reward agreement with ground truth on both benchmarks, suggesting this loop can operate without human annotation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 VLM 在扫描金融文档结构化抽取中无法提示字段错误的问题，提出把已有 token logprob 对齐到 JSON 中每个字段跨度以获得逐字段置信度，并用高不确定字段构造 GRPO 课程微调，同时以模型作伪标注判官。
AI.relevance_reason: 逐字段置信度与基于拒绝曲线的评估为「STOP」何时停止或弃答提供了可核查的廉价信号，但该方法不涉及 latent 推理状态的生成与使用，需核实其最小值 token 概率能否迁移到推理型多模态任务。
